Test Scenario: Verify successful authentication and canonical dashboard redirection across all four roles
Canonical Role(s): Employee, Grievance Staff, Department Head, Grievance Admin
Pre Conditions: Active synthetic user accounts exist for each role with valid passwords.
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to /login. 2. Enter email and password. 3. Click 'Sign In'. 4. Verify landing URL, dashboard KPI cards, and role badge.
Test Data (Synthetic): Synthetic credentials: emp.test@company.com, staff.hr@company.com, head.hr@company.com, admin@company.com
Expected Result: Authentication succeeds; redirected to role dashboard (/employee, /staff, /department-head, /admin); session cookie established.

Test Scenario: Boundary Verification: 4 failures don't lock; 5th failure within 15m locks for 15m; auto-unlocks after 15m
Pre Conditions: Active synthetic account (emp.lockout@company.com).
Test Steps: 1. Submit 4 incorrect passwords; verify account remains unlocked. 2. Submit 5th incorrect password within 15m; verify error 'Account is temporarily locked'. 3. Attempt 6th login immediately; verify rejected. 4. Advance time by 15 mins; submit correct password.
Expected Result: 4 failures keep account unlocked; 5th failure triggers 15-minute lockout; login during lockout rejected; account auto-unlocks after 15m.

Test Scenario: Boundary Verification: Authenticated user session expires after 30 minutes of continuous inactivity
Pre Conditions: Authenticated session active at T=0.
Test Steps: 1. Log in to dashboard. 2. Leave browser idle without interaction for 31 minutes. 3. Click 'My Grievances' or trigger API fetch.
Expected Result: Session invalidated; user intercepted with session expired notification and redirected to /login with return URL.

Test Scenario: Verify password change or reset invalidates all active sessions across all devices
Pre Conditions: Employee logged in simultaneously on Desktop Browser and Mobile Browser.
Test Steps: 1. On Desktop, navigate to /profile/security and change password. 2. On Mobile, click on grievance list to trigger API request.
Expected Result: Password update succeeds; Desktop session preserved or refreshed; Mobile session immediately invalidated with HTTP 401.

Test Scenario: Verify Employee cannot access another employee's grievance, and Staff/Head cannot access another department's grievance
Canonical Role(s): Employee A, Employee B, HR Staff, Finance Staff
Pre Conditions: Grievance G1 submitted by Emp A; Grievance G2 assigned to Finance.
Test Steps: 1. Log in as Emp B; attempt GET /api/end-user/grievances/[G1-id]. 2. Log in as HR Staff; attempt GET /api/staff/grievances/[G2-id].
Test Data (Synthetic): Emp B ID: 102 (Target G1: ID 101); HR Staff ID: 201 (Target G2: Finance ID 301)
Expected Result: Both requests return HTTP 403 Forbidden with access-denied message; zero cross-tenant data exposure.

Test Scenario: Verify end-to-end grievance submission with category taxonomy, evidence upload, and unique reference ID generation
Pre Conditions: Employee authenticated. Categories active.
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to /employee/submit. 2. Select Category & Subcategory. 3. Enter Title (>=5 chars) & Description (>=20 chars). 4. Attach PDF (2 MB). 5. Click Submit.
Test Data (Synthetic): Category: 'Compensation & Benefits'; Subcategory: 'Incorrect Deduction'; Title: 'Monthly PF Discrepancy'; File: 'payslip.pdf'
Expected Result: Grievance accepted; unique reference ID generated as GRS-YYYY-XXXX; record appears in tracking table in SUBMITTED status.

Test Scenario: Verify tracking hub, status tabs, search filters, and chronological audit timeline
Pre Conditions: Grievances exist across SUBMITTED, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, and CLOSED statuses.
Test Steps: 1. Log in as Employee. 2. Navigate to 'My Grievances'. 3. Switch between tabs (All, Active, Resolved, Closed). 4. Open case timeline.
Expected Result: Status tabs filter records accurately; timeline displays milestones with timestamps and actor attribution.

Test Scenario: Verify custom communication text displays verbatim across Employee, Staff, and Head dashboards
Pre Conditions: Grievance in IN_PROGRESS with information inquiry active.
Test Steps: 1. Employee opens communication feed; submits: 'Clarified deduction with bank statement.' 2. Log in as Staff & Head; inspect message.
Expected Result: Exact text renders verbatim across all dashboards; not overwritten by automated templates.

Test Scenario: Verify department queue ingestion and 100-point smart staff recommendation ranking
Pre Conditions: Grievance routed to department queue in AWAITING_ASSIGNMENT status. Eligible staff available.
Test Steps: 1. Log in as Department Head. 2. Open department queue. 3. Click 'Assign' on unassigned case. 4. Inspect recommendation modal ranking.
Expected Result: System calculates 100-pt advisory score (Skills 35, Exp 25, Workload 20, Avail 10, SLA 10); top recommendation ranked first; Head assigns Primary staff.

Test Scenario: Verify structured investigation findings documentation with non-numeric text validation
Pre Conditions: Grievance ASSIGNED in staff queue. Staff clicks 'Start Investigation'.
Test Steps: 1. Move status to IN_PROGRESS. 2. Attempt saving findings with pure numbers '9876543210' (negative test). 3. Enter valid narrative findings (>=20 chars). 4. Save findings.
Test Data (Synthetic): Negative: '9876543210'; Positive: 'Audited payroll ledger. Discrepancy caused by incorrect tax bracket configuration.'
Expected Result: Step 2 blocked with non-numeric validation error; Step 3 saves findings successfully in database.

Test Scenario: Verify strict department data isolation for internal department notes in multi-department cases
Canonical Role(s): Grievance Staff (Dept A), Grievance Staff (Dept B), Department Head
Pre Conditions: Multi-department case involving Dept A (Finance) and Dept B (HR).
Test Steps: 1. Dept A Staff adds private note in Internal Notes tab. 2. Log in as Dept B Staff on same case; inspect Internal Notes tab.
Test Data (Synthetic): Note Text: 'Confidential Finance internal audit: possible ledger error.'
Expected Result: Dept A Staff & Head view internal note. Dept B Staff & Head have zero access to Dept A internal notes (zero data leakage).

Sub Module: SLA Operational Indicators vs Lifecycle Status
Test Scenario: Verify ESCALATED (75%) and SLA_BREACHED (100%) are operational indicators and do NOT alter grievance lifecycle status
Pre Conditions: Grievance in IN_PROGRESS lifecycle status with active SLA tracking.
Test Steps: 1. Advance elapsed duration to 75% SLA; verify slaStatus updates to WARNING and Level 1 escalation logged. 2. Verify Grievance.status remains IN_PROGRESS. 3. Advance to 100% SLA; verify slaStatus updates to BREACHED. 4. Verify Grievance.status STILL remains IN_PROGRESS.
Expected Result: At 75% and 100%, operational SLA indicators update in tracking ledger; Grievance.status remains IN_PROGRESS throughout.

Test Scenario: Verify direct case ownership transfers automatically to Primary Department Head at 100% breach; Admin receives compliance alert only
Pre Conditions: Grievance assigned to staff member reaches 100% SLA duration.
Test Steps: 1. Advance SLA timer to 100% breach. 2. Inspect assignments table and active owner. 3. Verify in-app notifications sent to Head and Admin.
Expected Result: Direct case ownership transfers automatically to Primary Department Head; Grievance Admin receives compliance notice for institutional oversight only without taking ownership.

Test Scenario: Verify threshold notification dispatch boundaries: 50% to Staff only; 75% to Staff & Head; 100% to Staff, Head & Admin
Canonical Role(s): Grievance Staff, Department Head, Grievance Admin
Pre Conditions: Active grievance under monitoring.
Test Steps: 1. Advance timer to 50%; check notifications for Staff, Head, Admin. 2. Advance to 75%; check notifications. 3. Advance to 100%; check notifications.
Expected Result: At 50%: Staff only notified; Head/Admin not notified. At 75%: Staff and Head notified. At 100%: Staff, Head, and Admin notified.

Test Scenario: Verify SLA clock strictly pauses during AWAITING_CONFIRMATION (RESOLVED with resolutionStatus=PENDING_CONFIRMATION)
Pre Conditions: Investigation complete; Staff prepares final resolution.
Test Steps: 1. Staff submits final resolution. 2. Status moves to RESOLVED with resolutionStatus = PENDING_CONFIRMATION. 3. Advance wall clock by 48 hours. 4. Inspect active SLA timer.
Test Data (Synthetic): Wall clock elapsed: 48 hours while awaiting employee review
Expected Result: SLA clock remains paused and frozen at submission timestamp; zero elapsed SLA consumed during confirmation period.

Test Scenario: Verify SLA pause on AWAITING_INFORMATION and timer resume with remaining duration preserved upon clarification reply
Pre Conditions: Grievance in IN_PROGRESS with 10 hours elapsed out of 24h SLA.
Test Steps: 1. Staff requests clarification; status moves to AWAITING_INFORMATION. 2. Time advances 24h. 3. Employee submits requested info. 4. Status returns to IN_PROGRESS. 5. Inspect timer.
Test Data (Synthetic): Elapsed before pause = 10h; Paused duration = 24h; Wall clock = 34h
Expected Result: Timer paused during AWAITING_INFORMATION; upon employee reply, timer resumes with exactly 14h remaining (active elapsed = 10h, not 34h).

Test Scenario: Verify 7-day non-response to information request triggers automatic closure with INFORMATION_NOT_PROVIDED
Pre Conditions: Grievance in AWAITING_INFORMATION status.
Test Steps: 1. Staff requests info at T=0. 2. Verify reminder sent at T=6 days. 3. Advance time to T + 7 days 1 hour without employee reply. 4. Trigger background scheduler.
Expected Result: Grievance automatically transitions to CLOSED; closureReason set to 'INFORMATION_NOT_PROVIDED'; SLA remains permanently stopped.

Test Scenario: Verify 7-day complainant inactivity on proposed resolution triggers automatic closure with RESOLVED_INACTIVITY
Pre Conditions: Grievance in RESOLVED status with resolutionStatus = PENDING_CONFIRMATION.
Test Steps: 1. Staff submits resolution at T=0. 2. Verify reminder sent at T=6 days. 3. Advance time to T + 7 days 1 hour without employee response. 4. Run scheduler.
Expected Result: Grievance automatically transitions to CLOSED; closureReason set to 'RESOLVED_INACTIVITY'; feedback option enabled.

Test Scenario: Verify complainant resolution rejection moves case to REWORK, increments shared counter, and requires Head rework review
Pre Conditions: Grievance in PENDING_CONFIRMATION status. Shared attempt counter = 0.
Test Steps: 1. Employee clicks 'Request Rework'; provides reason (>=10 chars). 2. Case moves to REWORK; shared counter increments to 1. 3. Staff submits revised resolution. 4. Status moves to RESOLUTION_PENDING_APPROVAL (approvalType=REWORK). 5. Head approves.
Test Data (Synthetic): Rework Reason: 'Credited payroll adjustment missing overtime allowance.'
Expected Result: Case moves to REWORK; shared counter increments to 1; rework resolution requires Head approval; upon approval returns to RESOLVED (PENDING_CONFIRMATION).

Test Scenario: Boundary Verification: Reopening allowed on day 14 from closure; blocked on day 15
Pre Conditions: Grievance in CLOSED status. Shared attempt counter < 3.
Test Steps: 1. At T + 13 days 20h (day 14), Employee clicks 'Reopen Grievance'; submits valid reason; verify accepted into RESOLUTION_PENDING_APPROVAL. 2. On separate case at T + 14 days 2h (day 15), attempt reopening; verify blocked.
Test Data (Synthetic): Reopen Reason: 'Issue recurring after payroll adjustment.'
Expected Result: Day 14 request accepted for Department Head dispute review; Day 15 request rejected with 'Reopening period has expired'.

Test Scenario: Verify approved reopening initializes a fresh SLA cycle with the same priority default duration
Pre Conditions: Grievance in RESOLUTION_PENDING_APPROVAL (approvalType=REOPENAL_DISPUTE). Priority: Critical (24h).
Test Steps: 1. Department Head approves reopening dispute and assigns staff. 2. Status moves to REOPENED. 3. Inspect SLA tracking record.
Expected Result: Status transitions to REOPENED; fresh SLA cycle initialized with startedAt = now and deadline = now + 24h (same priority default, not separate 48h duration).

Test Scenario: Boundary Verification: 3rd attempt is allowed; 4th attempt is strictly rejected (not routed for manual review)
Pre Conditions: Grievance has undergone 2 reworks and 1 reopen (Shared count = 3). Grievance CLOSED.
Test Steps: 1. Employee opens closed case in tracking view. 2. Attempts submitting 4th reopen request with reason. 3. Inspect UI and API response.
Expected Result: System rejects 4th request with message 'Maximum combined attempt limit of 3 reached'; request rejected outright; not routed for manual review.

Test Scenario: Verify complainant satisfaction feedback capture upon resolution acceptance without altering CLOSED status
Pre Conditions: Grievance in PENDING_CONFIRMATION.
Test Steps: 1. Employee clicks 'Accept Resolution'. 2. Feedback modal prompts for rating (1-5) and comments. 3. Enter 5 stars and submit. 4. Verify case status.
Test Data (Synthetic): Rating: 5 Stars; Comments: 'Resolved quickly and accurately.'
Expected Result: Rating stored in grievance_feedback; grievance moves to CLOSED; feedback submission does NOT alter CLOSED status.

Test Scenario: Verify Grace Period workflow: eligible only when IN_PROGRESS & unbreached; max 1/cycle; max 2 lifecycle; cap <= min(24h, 25% SLA)
Pre Conditions: Grievance IN_PROGRESS, SLA unbreached, High priority (48h baseline).
Test Steps: 1. Staff requests 12h extension (25% of 48h). 2. Attempt requesting 16h (negative test: blocked). 3. Submit valid 12h request. 4. Head approves. 5. Attempt 2nd request in same cycle (blocked).
Expected Result: Extension <= 25% baseline accepted; Head approval extends deadline by 12h; max 1 request per cycle enforced strictly.

Test Scenario: Verify Supporting Department workflow: allocated SLA, deadline reminders, non-response notification to Primary Head, and conflict resolution
Canonical Role(s): Primary Head, Supporting Staff, Supporting Head, Grievance Admin
Pre Conditions: Multi-department case with Finance (Primary) and Facilities (Supporting).
Test Steps: 1. Facilities assigned with 40% duration. 2. Reminder dispatched before deadline. 3. Advance past deadline; verify Supporting Head and Primary Head alerted. 4. Primary Head requests Admin intervention on conflicting evidence.
Test Data (Synthetic): Primary: Finance; Supporting: Facilities (40% SLA allocation)
Expected Result: Supporting department tracked independently; non-response alerts Primary Head; Admin intervention coordinates conflict resolution.

Test Scenario: Verify deactivated staff members cannot receive assignments and active caseload triggers reassignment notification to Department Head
Pre Conditions: Staff member has 2 active assigned grievances.
Test Steps: 1. Admin deactivates staff account. 2. Verify staff blocked from logging in. 3. Verify Department Head receives notification to reassign the 2 active cases. 4. Head reassigns cases.
Expected Result: Staff account deactivated; login blocked; open grievances flagged for Head; Head reassigns cases successfully.

Test Scenario: Verify Admin configuration of categories, subcategories, and routing rules with inactive department guard
Pre Conditions: Admin authenticated at /admin/rules.
Test Steps: 1. Create new Category and Subcategory. 2. Map to Primary Department. 3. Attempt mapping to inactive department (negative test: blocked). 4. Submit grievance matching new category.
Test Data (Synthetic): New Category: 'Health & Wellness'; Subcategory: 'Ergonomic Support'; Department: 'Facilities'
Expected Result: Category created and immediately active; inactive department mapping rejected; grievance routes automatically to Facilities.

Test Scenario: Verify Admin configuration of priority SLA durations and thresholds (50% Warning, 75% Escalation, 100% Breach)
Pre Conditions: Admin authenticated at /admin/rules.
Test Steps: 1. Update High priority SLA duration. 2. Verify thresholds configured as 50%, 75%, 100%. 3. Submit new grievance; verify deadline reflects updated policy.
Expected Result: SLA policy saved; applies immediately to new grievances; in-flight grievances retain original calculated deadlines.

Test Scenario: Verify audit trail transactional consistency: failure to log audit record aborts and rolls back business operation
Pre Conditions: Admin attempting status or role assignment change.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger status change with audit logger active. 2. Verify audit record created with actor, timestamp, before/after state. 3. Simulate database audit write failure; verify status change is aborted.
Expected Result: Audit record committed atomically with business operation; failure in audit logging rolls back entire transaction.

Test Scenario: Verify automated rule-based recurrence clustering triggers alerts for Category Clustering (>7 in 30d) and Location Hotspots (>=3 in 30d)
Pre Conditions: Grievance records seeded over 30 calendar days.
Test Steps: 1. Seed 8 grievances in HR / Salary within 20 days. 2. Seed 3 grievances in Facilities sharing pincode 560001 within 15 days. 3. Open Analytics console.
Test Data (Synthetic): Category cluster: 8 HR cases; Hotspot: 3 cases at pincode 560001
Expected Result: System generates open RecurringGrievanceAlert for CATEGORY_CLUSTERING and LOCATION_HOTSPOT visible to Head and Admin.

Test Scenario: Verify operational volumes, Turnaround Time (TAT) analytics (average & median), and SLA compliance reporting
Pre Conditions: Completed and active grievances exist in database.
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to /admin/reports. 2. Filter by date range and department. 3. Inspect Average and Median TAT widgets. 4. Verify pending cases excluded from TAT.
Expected Result: Volumes, SLA compliance, and TAT calculated accurately; pending cases excluded from completed TAT.

Test Scenario: Verify report export to CSV and Excel with formula injection sanitization escaping (=, +, -, @)
Pre Conditions: Reports generated containing titles starting with formula characters '=cmd' or '+SUM'.
Test Steps: 1. Click 'Export to Excel' and 'Export to CSV'. 2. Open exported CSV in text editor. 3. Verify formula injection characters prefixed with single quote.
Test Data (Synthetic): Title in dataset: '=SUM(A1:B1) Payroll calculation error'
Expected Result: Export generates cleanly; formula injection characters escaped with leading single quote "'=SUM(A1:B1)".

Test Scenario: Boundary Verification: 10 MB size limit, max 5 attachments lifecycle, and executable blacklist
Pre Conditions: User on file attachment interface.
Test Steps: 1. Attempt uploading .exe, .sh, .bat files (rejected). 2. Attempt uploading 12 MB file (rejected). 3. Attempt uploading 6 files (rejected). 4. Upload valid 2 MB PDF (accepted).
Expected Result: Executable/script formats blocked; files >10MB blocked; >5 attachments blocked; valid PDF <=10MB accepted.

Test Scenario: Verify event-driven notifications, unread count badge, mark as read, and deep-link navigation
Pre Conditions: Lifecycle event triggered (case assigned, clarification requested, SLA warning).
Test Steps: 1. Log in as recipient. 2. Verify notification bell displays accurate unread badge count. 3. Click notification; verify deep-link navigates to specific grievance. 4. Mark notification as read.
Expected Result: Badge increments on event; clicking deep-links to grievance view; mark as read decrements badge count.

Test Scenario: Verify Department Head intervention controls are accessible immediately upon queue arrival (PENDING_ASSIGNMENT) and through escalation
Pre Conditions: Grievance in department queue.
Test Steps: 1. Head navigates to /department-head/queue. 2. Verify 'Intervene' action is active on unassigned case. 3. Reassign staff or take direct authority. 4. Verify case continues through escalation.
Expected Result: Intervention controls active immediately upon case arrival in queue and remain functional throughout escalation states.

Test Scenario: Verify sequential multi-department workflow isolates Department B SLA clock from Department A delay or breach
Canonical Role(s): Staff (Dept A), Staff (Dept B), Department Head
Pre Conditions: Sequential routing: Dept A (HR, 40% SLA), Dept B (Legal, 60% SLA).
Test Steps: 1. Dept A breaches its allocated 40% duration. 2. Dept A completes work and hands over to Dept B. 3. Inspect Dept B timer.
Test Data (Synthetic): Dept A: Breached 40% budget; Dept B: Sequential downstream recipient
Expected Result: Dept B activates upon handover with its full 100% promised time; Dept B is NOT marked breached and does not inherit Dept A delay.

Test Scenario: Verify end-to-end Knowledge Base workflow: Staff proposes KB article from closed grievance, Head approves, and similar recommendations display
Pre Conditions: Grievance in CLOSED status. Staff authenticated.
Test Steps: 1. Staff opens closed case; clicks 'Create KB Article'. 2. Duplicate check verifies similarity score. 3. Staff submits proposal. 4. Head reviews and approves article as PUBLISHED. 5. Staff on similar case views recommendation.
Test Data (Synthetic): Article: 'Payroll Tax Bracket Adjustment Resolution Guide'
Expected Result: Staff submits draft; duplicate check alerts if >90% match; Head publishes article; published article recommended on similar cases.

Test Scenario: Verify mandatory non-numeric validation on KB article rejection reason when Department Head rejects article
Pre Conditions: KB draft submitted for review.
Test Steps: 1. Head opens review view. 2. Attempts rejecting with pure numbers '12345678' (blocked). 3. Enters descriptive non-numeric feedback (>=15 chars). 4. Submits rejection.
Test Data (Synthetic): Negative: '12345678'; Positive: 'Insufficient explanation of ledger reconciliation steps.'
Expected Result: Pure numeric rejection reason blocked; valid descriptive feedback accepted and returned to staff.
